result.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
result.comment: 13 pages, 3 figures. Accepted as a poster at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Symmetry and Geometry in Neural Representations (NeurReps), Extended Abstract Track
result.summary: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. Using matched simulator and model responses, we measure action sensitivity with Gram matrices at three perturbation scales. Across nearly a thousand states from Reacher and OGBench Cube, the most sensitive action directions differ by median angles of about $36^\circ$ and $42^\circ$, respectively, at the smallest scale. Increasing the perturbation tenfold reduces median normalized Gram discrepancy by roughly 70\% on Reacher and 47\% on Cube. Geometry measured in pixels and embeddings varies more across scales than the chosen physical-state geometry. On held-out directions, environment Grams achieve median embedding response errors of 17\% and 28\%, compared with 26\% and 38\% for an isotropic reference with the same trace. LeWM's errors are higher at this scale. These findings support scale-specific evaluation of action sensitivity; its effect on control remains an open question.

AI.brief_summary: 论文检验预训练 LeWorldModel 是否保留局部动作几何：在 Reacher 与 OGBench Cube 上，用三种扰动尺度比较模拟器与模型的 Gram 矩阵、动作敏感方向及嵌入响应误差。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「多尺度扰动＋表示几何」诊断可能为核查 LVR/VLM 内部状态是否保留任务必要的局部结构提供思路，但研究对象是世界模型的动作敏感度，与推理期 latent 生成和使用的联系较间接。
